name: Information Complexity
definition: The **Information Complexity** of a hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}$ is the supremum, over sample sizes and data distributions, of the least mutual information $I(S;\mathcal{A}(S))$ between a sample $S$ and the output of a PAC-learning algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ for $\mathcal{H}$.
description: For arbitrary binary classes, finite information complexity is equivalent to finite Littlestone dimension. More quantitatively, finite Littlestone dimension $d$ implies $\mathrm{IC}(\mathcal H)\leq 2^d+\log_2(d+1)+3+3/(e\ln 2)$, by Pradeep, Nachum, and Gastpar. This is an exponential bound, so it is recorded here rather than as one of the graph's affine or logarithmic relationship edges.
graph_summary: Least worst-case mutual information between a training sample and a PAC learner's output. If $\mathrm{Ldim}=d$, then $\mathrm{IC}\leq2^d+\log_2(d+1)+3+3/(e\ln2)$.
origin_references: Defined in this form by Pradeep, Nachum, and Gastpar \cite{pradeep2022information}.

monotonic.proof: A PAC learner for $\mathcal H$ is also a PAC learner for a subfamily $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$. Using the same learner does not increase $I(S;\mathcal A(S))$, so taking the infimum over learners and supremum over distributions preserves the inequality.

p_monotonic.proof: Let $\mathcal R=\mathcal H|_T$ be a coordinate projection. For any PAC learner $\mathcal A$ for $\mathcal H$, run $\mathcal A$ on a sample supported on $T$ (viewed as a sample on the original domain) and output $\mathcal A(S)|_T$. Every target in $\mathcal R$ has an extension in $\mathcal H$, so this PAC learns $\mathcal R$. By data processing, $I(S;\mathcal A(S)|_T)\leq I(S;\mathcal A(S))$. Taking the infimum over learners and the required suprema proves $\mathrm{IC}(\mathcal R)\leq\mathrm{IC}(\mathcal H)$.

c_monotonic.proof: For a conditioned class, first take the subfamily $\mathcal G=\{h\in\mathcal H:h|_S=y\}$ and then project away $S$. Subfamily monotonicity followed by projection monotonicity gives $\mathrm{IC}(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm{IC}(\mathcal G)\geq\mathrm{IC}(\mathcal H_{S=y})$.

doubly_monotonic.proof: This is the conjunction of the established subfamily- and projection-monotonicity arguments.
